metadata.description: Personal Claude Code skills by João Vogler — code review, PR workflow, planning, writing, and frontend architecture.

plugins.name: frontend
plugins.description: Use when adding or changing a feature, page, API call, hook, form, or component in a React or Next.js app laid out as infrastructure + domain + view + routes; when deciding which layer code belongs in; when reviewing a diff for layering violations; or when structuring a greenfield frontend. Covers dependency rules, naming, serialization boundaries, and typed errors.

plugins.name: plan
plugins.description: Use when planning a new feature, refactor, package upgrade, migration, or design, architecture, or infrastructure change — and when executing the resulting plan. `plan:write` produces a phased plan file with explicit requirements, alternatives, and tests; `plan:execute` runs one phase, a span, or the whole plan under code writing standards, marking tasks complete and committing each phase.

plugins.name: pr
plugins.description: Use when working a pull request end to end: reviewing a diff locally for real bugs and design problems without posting anything to GitHub, and writing a PR description that explains why the change exists instead of narrating the diff file by file.

plugins.name: writing
plugins.description: Use when editing or reviewing prose to strip the signs of AI-generated writing and make it read as human-written. Based on Wikipedia's "Signs of AI writing" guide: inflated symbolism, promotional language, superficial -ing analyses, vague attributions, em dash overuse, rule of three, AI vocabulary, passive voice, negative parallelisms, and filler phrases.
